checks.double_registration: The constructor call (PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp:85) remains; INITIALIZE_PASS wraps the registration in llvm::call_once, so the second call is a no-op. Build has LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON and no duplicate-registration assertion fired in any run. -debug-pass=Structure at -O0 and -O2 lists 'PULP Hardware Loop Fixup' exactly once, same as the int-20 llc.
checks.static_vs_shared: Tree is configured static (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF, no dylib); a shared build was not built (too expensive on the loaded host). checks.start_after_limitation: Confirmed: -start-after=hwloopsfixup assembly fails in llvm-mc with 'Undefined temporary symbol .LBB0_3/.LBB0_4/.LBB0_9'. Diff against -start-before output shows exactly the lp.setup end-label block printed as '# %bb.N' instead of '.LBB0_N: # Label of block must be emitted'. At llvmorg-20.1.8 MachineBasicBlock::LabelMustBeEmitted is not serialized by MIRPrinter/MIRParser (git grep finds it only in MachineBasicBlock.h/.cpp, AsmPrinter.cpp, SelectionDAGBuilder.cpp); the fork sets it at PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp:746,867, PULPHardwareLoops.cpp:1598, SNITCHFrepLoops.cpp:561. The loop-header label survives because it is serialized as machine-block-address-taken. Not blocking: before this change -start-after was not reachable at all, normal compilation is unchanged, and -run-pass/-stop-after MIR tests work. Already tracked as BACKLOG B122 (open).
